examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 살가죽이 얼얼해요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day and my skin is tingling.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 너무 말라서 뼈에 살가죽만 붙어 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: He is so thin that it looks like there is only skin on his bones.

examples.ko: 닭고기는 살가죽을 벗기고 먹는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to eat chicken with the skin removed.

examples.ko: 할아버지 손은 살가죽이 늘어져서 주름이 많아요.
examples.en: Grandpa's hands have loose skin and a lot of wrinkles.
I got bitten by a bug and my skin swelled up red.

examples.ko: 살가죽 한 겹 아래에 핏줄이 다 보여요.
examples.en: You can see all the veins just under the skin.

explain: '피부'가 가장 평범한 말이고, '살가죽'은 얇은 껍질처럼 거칠고 늘어진 느낌으로 말할 때 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 닭이나 동물의 껍질에도 쓰고, 말투가 조금 투박해서 '피부'나 '살갗'처럼 부드럽게 들리지는 않아요.
explain_en: '피부' is the plain everyday word, while '살가죽' sounds rough, like a thin loose covering. It is used for people and also for the skin of chickens and animals, and it sounds blunter than '피부' or '살갗'.

examples.en: My skin got sunburned and it stings.
The cold wind touched my skin and I got goosebumps.
A baby's skin is really soft.
A mosquito bit my skin and it keeps itching.
My skin was chapped, so I put cream on it.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물에 살갗을 데어서 많이 아파요.
examples.en: I burned my skin with hot water and it really hurts.

explain: '피부'보다 몸 겉에 닿는 느낌(바람, 햇볕, 아픔)을 말할 때 자주 어울려요. 그래서 '살갗이 따갑다', '살갗에 닿다'처럼 감각과 함께 많이 써요. '살가죽'보다 부드럽고 자연스러운 말이에요.
explain_en: Compared with '피부', it fits well when you talk about what the body surface feels, such as wind, sun or pain. So you often see '살갗이 따갑다' or '살갗에 닿다'. It sounds softer and more natural than '살가죽'.

en: skin; skin texture; color of complexion

examples.ko: 부드러운 살결을 가지고 싶어서 로션을 매일 발라요.
examples.en: I want soft skin, so I put on lotion every day.
That child has fine, fair skin.
My skin got rough, so I put on a face mask.
It's a blanket as soft as a baby's skin.
Your skin looks clear and translucent these days.
In winter, skin easily gets dry.

explain: '살결'은 피부의 겉 모양이나 감촉, 곱고 거친 정도를 말할 때 써요. '곱다, 거칠다, 보드랍다, 희다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 피부 상태를 얘기할 때 '피부결'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: '살결' is for how skin looks and feels, whether it is fine or rough. It pairs well with words like 곱다, 거칠다, 보드랍다 and 희다. People also say '피부결' when talking about skin condition.

en: way of livelihood; way of living

examples.en: I have no job, so I have no idea how to get by.
We have to find a way to survive somehow.

examples.ko: 공장이 문을 닫아서 직원들의 살길이 걱정돼요.
examples.en: The factory closed, so I worry about how the workers will make a living.
Our only way to survive is to work hard.
In the old countryside, farming was the way to make a living.
I often heard people say that exports are the key to survival.

explain: 먹고살 방법이나 어려움을 벗어날 길을 말해요. '살길이 막막하다', '살길을 찾다', '~이/가 살길이다'처럼 자주 써요. 개인의 생계뿐 아니라 회사나 나라가 버틸 방법에도 써요.
explain_en: It means a way to make a living or a way out of hardship. Common patterns are '살길이 막막하다', '살길을 찾다' and '~이/가 살길이다'. It applies to a person's livelihood and also to a company or country's way to survive.

examples.en: My mom is a really thrifty homemaker.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 살림꾼이라서 집이 늘 깨끗해요.
examples.en: She's good at housekeeping, so her home is always clean.
I met a wife who runs the home well, so I have no worries.

examples.ko: 살림꾼으로 소문난 이모가 반찬을 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: My aunt, known as a great homemaker, sent me side dishes.

examples.ko: 저는 살림꾼이 못 돼서 요리도 서툴러요.
examples.en: I'm not much of a homemaker, so I'm clumsy at cooking too.
He plays the role of the one who keeps things running at the company too.

explain: 집안일과 돈 관리를 야무지게 잘하는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요. 여자만이 아니라 남자에게도 쓰고, 회사나 모임의 일을 꼼꼼하게 챙기는 사람에게도 비유로 말해요.
explain_en: It praises someone who handles housework and household money well. It is used for men as well as women, and also figuratively for someone who takes care of the details in a company or group.

examples.en: I bought the household items needed for our new home one by one.
When I moved, I threw away a lot of old household goods.
Prices have gone up lately, so making ends meet is hard.
We aren't well off, but we live happily.

examples.ko: 그 집은 살림살이가 단출해서 깔끔해 보여요.
examples.en: That house has few belongings, so it looks neat.

examples.ko: 올해는 우리 동네 살림살이가 많이 나아졌어요.
examples.en: This year, life in our neighborhood has improved a lot.

explain: 집에서 쓰는 가구나 그릇 같은 물건을 말할 때도 있고, 생활 형편을 말할 때도 있어요. '살림살이가 나아지다/어렵다'처럼 형편을 말할 때 자주 써요. 줄여서 '살림'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It can mean household things such as furniture and dishes, or a household's financial situation. For the second meaning, phrases like '살림살이가 나아지다' or '살림살이가 어렵다' are common. It is often shortened to '살림'.

en: the pleasure of living; something to live for

examples.en: Being with my family makes life feel worth living.

examples.ko: 요즘은 일이 너무 힘들어서 살맛이 안 나요.
examples.en: Work is so hard these days that I don't feel any joy in life.
Thanks to my friend, I found joy in life again.
My pay went up, so life feels good.

examples.ko: 모두가 살맛 나는 세상을 만들고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to make a world where everyone enjoys life.
Eating something delicious makes life feel good.

explain: 기분 좋은 일이 있을 때는 '살맛이 나다', 힘들고 의욕이 없을 때는 '살맛이 안 나다'라고 해요. '사는 재미'보다 입말에 가깝고, 거창한 행복보다 소소한 즐거움에 어울려요. 심각하게 죽고 싶다는 말은 아니에요.
explain_en: When something good happens you say '살맛이 나다', and when you are worn out and unmotivated, '살맛이 안 나다'. It sounds more spoken than '사는 재미' and fits small joys better than grand happiness. It does not mean you are seriously suicidal.

examples.en: Her skin is fair and clear.
I got tanned and my skin tone became much darker.

examples.ko: 이 파운데이션은 제 살빛에 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: This foundation suits my skin tone well.
The baby's skin is a lovely pink.

examples.ko: 살빛이 창백해서 병원에 가 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: Your skin looks pale, so I told you to see a doctor.
I bought stockings in a color close to my skin tone.

explain: '피부색'이 일상에서 더 평범하고, '살빛'은 조금 부드럽고 글 같은 느낌이에요. 예전에 '살색'이라고 하던 색은 지금은 '살구색'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: '피부색' is the more ordinary word, and '살빛' sounds a little softer and more literary. The color once called '살색' is now called '살구색'.

examples.en: A thin layer of ice formed at the edge of the lake.

examples.ko: 아침에 길에 살얼음이 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: There is thin ice on the road this morning, so be careful.
Cold noodles with a thin layer of ice are really refreshing.
I drank sikhye with thin ice floating in it.

examples.ko: 밤새 기온이 내려가서 물웅덩이에 살얼음이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The temperature dropped overnight and thin ice formed on the puddle.
Please eat it quickly before the slush melts.

explain: 얇게 살짝 언 얼음을 말해요. 겨울 길이나 호수뿐 아니라 살얼음이 낀 냉면, 식혜처럼 음식에도 자주 써요. '살얼음이 잡히다/끼다/얼다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 시험 결과를 기다리는 내내 살얼음판을 걷는 기분이었어요.
phrases.en: I felt like I was walking on thin ice the whole time I waited for the test results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 얼음이 아니라, 언제 일이 틀어질지 몰라 몹시 조마조마한 상황을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about real ice. It describes a very tense situation where things could go wrong at any moment.

explain_en: It means a thin, light layer of ice. Besides winter roads and lakes, it is often used for food, such as cold noodles or sikhye with a thin icy layer. Say '살얼음이 잡히다/끼다/얼다'.

examples.en: He is well built, so he looks reliable.

examples.ko: 요즘 운동을 안 했더니 살집이 많이 붙었어요.
examples.en: I haven't exercised lately and I've put on a lot of weight.
I walk every day to lose some body fat.

examples.ko: 이 부위는 살집이 많아서 맛이 부드러워요.
examples.en: This cut has a lot of meat, so it tastes tender.
Grandma is a bit plump, so being hugged by her feels cozy.
I've put on some weight and my clothes are tight.

explain: 몸에 살이 붙은 정도나 두툼함을 말해요. '뚱뚱하다'보다 덜 직접적이라 '살집이 있다'로 부드럽게 말할 때가 많아요. 생선이나 고기의 두툼한 부분을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes how much flesh the body has. It is less direct than '뚱뚱하다', so people often say '살집이 있다' to be gentle. It also describes the thick, meaty part of fish or meat.

examples.ko: 곰은 겨울이 오기 전에 열심히 먹고 몸을 살찌워요.
examples.en: Bears eat a lot and fatten up before winter comes.
We give the cows more feed to fatten them up.
I work hard making baby food to help the baby gain weight.

examples.ko: 많이 먹는다고 무조건 살찌우는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Eating a lot doesn't necessarily make you gain weight.
The farmer fattens the livestock and puts them on the market.
The tourism industry enriched the local economy.

explain: '살찌다'는 스스로 살이 오르는 것이고, '살찌우다'는 누군가를 살찌게 만드는 말이에요. 그래서 '나는 살쪘어요'라고 하고 '살찌웠어요'는 쓰지 않아요. '경제를 살찌우다'처럼 더 풍요롭게 한다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: '살찌다' is to gain weight by oneself, while '살찌우다' means to make someone or something gain weight. So you say '살쪘어요' for yourself, not '살찌웠어요'. It is also used figuratively, as in '경제를 살찌우다' (to enrich the economy).

examples.en: Lean meat is lighter in taste than pork belly.
Chicken breast is lean meat with little fat.
I picked only the lean meat and put it in the curry.
I cut off the fat and ate the lean meat.
This sausage has a high lean meat content.
The child likes fat more than lean meat.

explain: 뼈와 기름을 뺀 붉은 고기 부분이에요. 반대말은 '비계'(기름 부분)예요. 식당이나 정육점에서 '살코기로 주세요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is the red meat part without bone or fat. The opposite is '비계' (the fatty part). At a restaurant or butcher you might say '살코기로 주세요'.

examples.ko: 그 드라마는 세 사람의 삼각관계가 중심이에요.
examples.en: That drama centers on a love triangle among three people.

examples.ko: 친구와 같은 사람을 좋아해서 삼각관계가 됐어요.
examples.en: My friend and I like the same person, so it turned into a love triangle.

examples.ko: 삼각관계 때문에 두 사람 사이가 멀어졌어요.
examples.en: The love triangle drove the two of them apart.

examples.ko: 영화 속 삼각관계가 너무 뻔해서 재미없었어요.
examples.en: The love triangle in the movie was so predictable that it wasn't fun.

examples.ko: 저는 삼각관계에 얽히는 건 정말 싫어요.
examples.en: I really hate getting caught up in a love triangle.

examples.ko: 세 나라의 삼각관계가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The three-way relationship among the three countries often appears in the news.

explain: 주로 세 사람 사이의 연애 갈등을 말해서 드라마나 영화에 자주 나와요. 연애뿐 아니라 세 나라나 세 회사처럼 서로 얽힌 세 쪽의 관계에도 써요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to romantic tension among three people, a common topic in dramas and movies. It also covers any three-way relationship, such as among three countries or companies.

examples.en: Korea is surrounded by the sea on three sides.

examples.ko: 이 방은 삼면에 창문이 있어서 밝아요.
examples.en: This room has windows on three sides, so it is bright.
The village has mountains on three sides, so there is little wind.

examples.ko: 삼면 거울 앞에서 옷을 입어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried on clothes in front of a three-panel mirror.
Three sides of the building are made of glass.
It is closed on three sides, so sound echoes.

explain: '우리나라는 삼면이 바다다'처럼 한국 지리를 말할 때 가장 많이 나와요. 네 쪽이면 '사면'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 '세 면'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It appears most in the Korean geography sentence '우리나라는 삼면이 바다다'. With four sides it is '사면', and in daily speech people also say '세 면'.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 노래, 춤, 외모 삼박자를 다 갖췄어요.
examples.en: That singer has all three: singing, dancing and looks.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 맛, 가격, 분위기 삼박자가 맞아요.
examples.en: This restaurant gets all three right: taste, price and atmosphere.
A waltz is usually danced to a triple-time rhythm.

examples.ko: 삼박자가 딱 맞아서 일이 잘 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Everything fell into place, so the work went well.
I walked slowly to a song in triple time.

examples.ko: 공부, 운동, 인성까지 삼박자를 갖춘 학생이에요.
examples.en: He is a student who has it all: studies, sports and character.

explain: 원래는 음악의 3박 리듬을 말해요. 일상에서는 세 가지 조건이 모두 잘 맞는다는 비유로 더 많이 써요. 보통 '삼박자를 갖추다', '삼박자가 맞다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 집은 위치, 가격, 크기 삼박자를 갖췄어요.
phrases.en: This house has it all: location, price and size.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악 용어가 아니라, 중요한 세 가지 조건이 다 좋다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about music. It praises something that has three important qualities all in good shape.

explain_en: Originally it is the three-beat rhythm in music. In daily talk it is used more often figuratively for three conditions all lining up well. Typical forms are '삼박자를 갖추다' and '삼박자가 맞다'.

examples.en: Grandpa likes to wear hemp clothes in summer.
Hemp clothes let air through well, so they are cool.
Hemp clothes are rough, but they are good in hot weather.
I looked at old hemp clothes at the museum.
My mother washed the hemp clothes by hand for me.
I received a set of hemp clothes as a gift.

explain: '삼베'는 삼으로 짠 천이고, '삼베옷'은 그 천으로 만든 옷이에요. 올이 거칠고 통풍이 잘돼서 여름 옷감으로 알려져 있어요. 한복 이야기를 할 때 '모시옷'과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '삼베' is cloth woven from hemp, and '삼베옷' is clothing made of it. It has a coarse weave and breathes well, so it is known as a summer fabric. It often appears together with '모시옷' when talking about hanbok.

examples.en: My older brother retook the exam a third time to get into college.
After a third attempt, I finally passed.

examples.ko: 삼수까지 하는 건 쉬운 결정이 아니에요.
examples.en: Going for a third try is not an easy decision.
My third-attempt year was very hard.

examples.ko: 삼수 중인 친구에게 응원 문자를 보냈어요.
examples.en: I sent an encouraging text to my friend who is on a third attempt.
When you go for a third try, you feel very anxious.

explain: 대학 입시에서 두 번 떨어지고 세 번째로 도전하는 것을 말해요. 한 번만 다시 도전하면 '재수'라고 해서, 재수·삼수처럼 짝으로 써요. 보통 '삼수를 하다', '삼수 끝에'로 말해요.
explain_en: In college entrance exams it means taking the exam a third time after failing twice. Retaking it just once is '재수', so the two are used as a pair. Typical forms are '삼수를 하다' and '삼수 끝에'.

en: have a third try; make three attempts

examples.en: That friend is trying a third time to get into medical school.
I got into the school I wanted on my third try.
I decided to get a job instead of trying a third time.

examples.ko: 삼수할 생각이 있으면 미리 계획을 세우세요.
examples.en: If you plan to try a third time, make a plan in advance.
My older sister went to a cram school while she was on her third try.
I took a third try, but I have no regrets.

explain: '삼수'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사로, 입시를 세 번째 치른다는 뜻이에요. 한 번 덜 했으면 '재수하다'라고 해요. 시험 이야기에서 '삼수생'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: This is the verb form of '삼수', meaning to take an entrance exam for the third time. With one fewer attempt it is '재수하다'. People also say '삼수생' for a student on a third try.

examples.en: Red, blue and yellow are the three primary colors.
The three primary colors of light are red, green and blue.

examples.ko: 삼원색을 섞으면 여러 가지 색이 나와요.
examples.en: Mixing the three primary colors makes many different colors.
In art class, I drew a picture using the three primary colors.
A TV screen also makes colors from three primary colors.

examples.ko: 삼원색이 뭔지 설명해 줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can you explain what the three primary colors are?

explain: 물감과 빛은 삼원색이 달라요. 학교에서는 물감의 빨강, 파랑, 노랑을 배우고, 화면의 빛은 빨강, 초록, 파랑이에요. 어느 쪽 이야기인지 같이 말해 주면 헷갈리지 않아요.
explain_en: Paint and light have different primaries. At school you learn red, blue and yellow for paint, while light on a screen uses red, green and blue. Mentioning which one you mean avoids confusion.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 삼차원 화면으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can watch this movie in three dimensions.
I made a small doll with a 3D printer.
A map is flat, and a globe is three-dimensional.

examples.ko: 삼차원 공간에는 길이, 너비, 높이가 있어요.
examples.en: Three-dimensional space has length, width and height.
I find the picture that looks three-dimensional amazing.

examples.ko: 그 게임은 삼차원 그래픽이 아주 좋아요.
examples.en: That game has really good 3D graphics.

explain: 일상에서는 영어 그대로 '3D(쓰리디)'라고 더 많이 말해요. '삼차원'은 수업이나 설명에서 잘 나오고, 반대말은 '이차원'이나 '평면'이에요.
explain_en: In daily speech people more often say '3D' (쓰리디) in English. '삼차원' shows up in lessons and explanations, and its opposites are '이차원' and '평면'.

examples.en: Tonight I ate grilled Spanish mackerel with my family.

examples.ko: 삼치는 살이 부드러워서 아이들도 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Spanish mackerel has soft flesh, so even kids eat it well.
I bought two Spanish mackerel at the market.
My mom braised Spanish mackerel in soy sauce for me.

examples.ko: 삼치 한 토막에 밥 한 공기면 충분해요.
examples.en: One piece of Spanish mackerel and a bowl of rice is enough.
The fish shop cleaned the Spanish mackerel for me.

explain: 고등어, 갈치처럼 집밥 반찬으로 먹는 생선이에요. 구이나 조림으로 많이 먹고, 식당 메뉴에서는 '삼치구이'로 자주 봐요.
explain_en: Like mackerel and hairtail, it is a fish eaten as a home-cooked side dish. It is often grilled or braised, and on restaurant menus you often see '삼치구이'.

examples.en: I made an acrostic poem with my friend's name.

examples.ko: 삼행시 짓기 놀이를 하면 웃음이 터져요.
examples.en: When we play the acrostic game, everyone bursts out laughing.

examples.ko: 제 이름으로 삼행시 한번 해 볼래요?
examples.en: Do you want to try an acrostic with my name?

examples.ko: 국어 시간에 삼행시 쓰기 숙제가 있었어요.
examples.en: In Korean class, we had a homework assignment to write an acrostic.
That acrostic is really witty.
Please pick a title for the acrostic.

explain: 세 글자 단어나 이름의 글자를 한 줄의 첫 글자로 삼아 세 줄로 짓는 말놀이예요. 친구 이름이나 '고구마' 같은 말로 하면서 웃음을 주고받아요. 글자 수에 따라 사행시, 오행시도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a word game where each letter of a three-letter word or name starts one of three lines. People do it with a friend's name or a word like '고구마' for laughs. With more letters you get 사행시 or 오행시.

examples.en: The older girls from higher grades helped the new students.

examples.ko: 저는 상급생이 되면 동아리 회장을 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: When I become an upperclassman, I want to be club president.
He is a junior who greets his seniors well.
The upperclassmen are playing soccer on the playground.
We are doing this event together with the upperclassmen.
Do you know anyone among the upperclassmen?

explain: 학년이 더 높은 학생을 말하고 반대말은 '하급생'이에요. 말할 때는 같은 학교의 학년이 높은 사람을 '선배'라고 더 자주 불러요. '상급생'은 학교 소개나 글에서 학년 차이를 설명할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It means a student in a higher grade, and its opposite is '하급생'. In conversation, people more often call a higher-grade student at the same school '선배'. '상급생' fits when explaining grade differences in school descriptions or writing.

examples.en: It's a holiday, so we set out so much food the table nearly bent.
The table leg was wobbly, so I stuck a book under it.
Grandma laid out a feast so big the table could break.
I folded the table legs and put the table in the storage room.

examples.ko: 이 상은 상다리가 접혀서 보관이 편해요.
examples.en: This table has folding legs, so it is easy to store.
I tripped on the table leg and almost fell.

explain: 여기서 '상'은 밥을 차려 먹는 작은 상이에요. 앉을 때 다리 모양인 '책상다리'(양반다리)와는 달라요. 잔칫상이나 명절 음식 이야기에서 관용 표현으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 손님이 온다고 어머니가 상다리가 부러지게 차리셨어요.
phrases.en: Because guests were coming, my mother laid out a huge feast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상다리가 진짜 부러진다는 게 아니라, 음식을 아주 푸짐하게 많이 차렸다는 과장된 표현이에요. '상다리가 휘어지게'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The table leg does not really break. It is an exaggeration for setting out a huge amount of food. '상다리가 휘어지게' is also used.

explain_en: Here '상' is the small table where meals are served. It is different from '책상다리', which is the cross-legged sitting posture. It often appears in an idiom about holiday or feast food.

examples.en: We keep medicine at home, so I took a headache pill.
Pack some basic medicine when you travel.
You can buy basic medicines at a convenience store.
I keep cold medicine and a digestive aid ready as basic medicine.

examples.ko: 상비약 상자를 정리하니 유통기한이 지난 약이 많았어요.
examples.en: When I tidied the medicine box, many pills were past their expiry date.

examples.ko: 상비약은 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep basic medicine out of children's reach.

explain: 열이나 두통, 소화불량처럼 갑자기 필요할 때를 위해 집이나 가방에 늘 두는 약이에요. 병원에서 받은 처방약이 아니라 약국이나 편의점에서 쉽게 사는 약을 말해요. '구급약'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is medicine you always keep at home or in a bag for sudden needs, like fever, headache or indigestion. It refers to easy over-the-counter medicine, not prescriptions from a hospital. It is sometimes used much like '구급약'.

examples.ko: 상속세 때문에 집을 팔았다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that someone sold their house because of inheritance tax.

examples.ko: 상속세는 물려받는 재산이 많을수록 더 많이 내요.
examples.en: The more property you inherit, the more inheritance tax you pay.

examples.ko: 부모님 재산을 받으면 상속세를 내야 해요.
examples.en: If you receive your parents' assets, you have to pay inheritance tax.
Don't miss the deadline for filing the inheritance tax.

examples.ko: 그 부자는 상속세만 수십억 원을 냈어요.
examples.en: That rich person paid billions of won in inheritance tax alone.
The government announced a plan to reduce the inheritance tax.

explain: 세상을 떠난 사람의 재산을 물려받을 때 내는 세금이에요. 살아 있는 사람이 미리 주는 경우에는 '증여세'라고 해서 둘이 짝으로 자주 나와요. 주로 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 들어요.
explain_en: It is the tax paid when receiving the property of someone who has died. When a living person gives property in advance, it is called '증여세', and the two often appear as a pair. You mostly hear it in news and economic talk.

examples.en: That doesn't make sense by common sense.
A sensible person wouldn't do that.
Please sell it at a reasonable price.
I think that kind of request is reasonable.

examples.ko: 그 사장의 행동은 전혀 상식적이지 않아요.
examples.en: That boss's behavior is not sensible at all.
Let's talk at a reasonable level.

explain: 사전에서는 관형사로 나오지만 실제로는 '상식적인 사람', '상식적으로', '상식적이다'처럼 활용해서 써요. 누군가의 행동이나 요구가 보통 사람이 생각하는 선인지 따질 때 많이 말해요. 반대는 '비상식적'이에요.
explain_en: The dictionary lists it as a determiner, but in practice it is used as '상식적인 사람', '상식적으로' or '상식적이다'. People use it to judge whether someone's behavior or demand fits what ordinary people consider normal. The opposite is '비상식적'.

examples.ko: 그 축제는 너무 상업화돼서 예전 분위기가 없어요.
examples.en: That festival has become so commercialized that the old atmosphere is gone.

examples.ko: 관광지가 상업화되는 것을 걱정하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people worry about tourist spots becoming commercialized.
He founded a company to commercialize the research results.
Only products that succeed in commercialization remain on the market.
It is a neighborhood where commercialization is moving fast.
The music was criticized for being too commercialized.

explain: 돈을 버는 것이 중심이 되도록 바뀌는 것을 말해서, 비판하는 느낌으로 자주 쓰여요. '상품화'는 물건이나 서비스로 만들어 파는 것에 더 중립적으로 써요. '상업화되다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means changing so that making money becomes the main focus, and it often carries a critical tone. '상품화' is more neutral and means turning something into a product to sell. '상업화되다' is a very common form.

examples.en: There are many shops in my neighborhood's shopping street.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에도 지붕 있는 상점가는 걸을 만해요.
examples.en: A covered shopping street is fine to walk even on rainy days.
I bought fruit and side dishes at the shopping street.
The shopping street in front of the station is crowded every weekend.

examples.ko: 상점가 사장님들이 함께 할인 행사를 열었어요.
examples.en: The shop owners on the street held a discount event together.
There are many cafes in the newly opened shopping street.

explain: 가게들이 길을 따라 모여 있는 거리나 지역을 말해요. 건물 안에 가게가 모인 곳은 '상가'라고 하는 경우가 많고, 큰 시장은 '시장'이라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '가게 거리'나 '상가'를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means a street or area where shops are gathered along the road. A place where shops are inside a building is often called '상가', and a big market is '시장'. In casual talk you may hear '상가' more often.

examples.en: I fell and my knees were covered in scrapes.
I held the cat and now my hands are covered in scratches.

examples.ko: 축구를 하고 온 아들은 온몸이 상처투성이였어요.
examples.en: My son came back from soccer with scrapes all over his body.
His heart is already full of wounds.
I walked to the end on my badly scarred feet.
I took my scratched-up car in for repair.

explain: '-투성이'는 어떤 것이 가득 묻거나 많은 모양을 나타내요. '흙투성이', '먼지투성이', '피투성이'처럼 쓰여요. 몸뿐 아니라 마음이나 물건에도 비유로 말해요.
explain_en: '-투성이' shows that something is covered with or full of a thing, as in '흙투성이', '먼지투성이' and '피투성이'. It can be used for bodies and also figuratively for hearts or objects.

examples.en: I won the competition and received a plaque.

examples.ko: 사무실 선반에 상패가 쭉 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A row of plaques sits on the office shelf.
The company gave me a plaque for long service.
My father polished the plaque and put it in the living room.
My name is engraved incorrectly on the plaque.
I received prize money along with the plaque.

explain: 나무나 금속에 글자를 새겨서 주는 상이에요. 종이로 주는 것은 '상장', 컵 모양은 '트로피'라고 해서 구분해요. 보통 '상패를 받다/수여하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is an award made of wood or metal with writing engraved on it. A paper certificate is '상장' and a cup-shaped award is '트로피', so they are distinguished. Typical forms are '상패를 받다' and '상패를 수여하다'.

examples.en: It took a year for that idea to become a product.
They are turning local specialties into products and selling them.
When the character became popular, it was turned into merchandise right away.

examples.ko: 상품화에 성공하면 큰돈을 벌 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the productization succeeds, you can make a lot of money.
This technology hasn't been turned into a product yet.
The design changed a lot during the productization process.

explain: 아이디어, 기술, 캐릭터 같은 것을 팔 수 있는 물건이나 서비스로 만드는 것을 말해요. '상업화'보다 중립적이고, 비판하는 느낌은 적어요. 보통 '상품화하다/상품화되다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It means turning an idea, technology or character into a product or service that can be sold. It is more neutral than '상업화' and carries less criticism. Typical forms are '상품화하다' and '상품화되다'.
